newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest spot electricity mostly steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest spot electricity mostly steady to lower.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. were mostly steady to lower with expectations of some moderation in frigid temperatures on Wednesday, power brokers and marketers said.

Forecasts called for a more southerly flow of warmer air to ease cold in much of the Mid-West tomorrow, through temperatures were expected to take another downturn Thursday and Friday to 10 to 15 degrees Fahrenheit below normal.
Some possible moderation in the cold was seen by Saturday.

In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), where temperatures continued to be extremely cold, peak, non-firm power prices for Wednesday delivery were discussed higher at $36.00-39.00 from $34.00-37.00 on Monday.
Off-peak next day non-firm MAPP power was talked over a wider range of $14.00-18.00 from $15.00-17.00 on Monday for Tuesday delivery, the sources said.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Wednesday were talked lower in the $26.00-28.00 range from $35.00-39.00 on Monday.
Sources said that despite the cold temperatures the vast majority of electricity generating units continued to function well with few constraints on power deliveries.
MAIN off peak next day power eased slightly to $16.00-18.00 from $16.50-18.50 on Monday, the sources said.
Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Wednesday eased to $26.00-29.00 from $35.00-38.00 per MWh.
ECAR electricity prices for off-peak, non-firm delivery were assessed steady to lower at $15.00-18.00 from a notional assessment at $15.00-19.00 on Monday.
February ECAR was said to have eased to near $23.50-24.00 from $23.75-24.25 on Monday.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) peak, non-firm power prices for Wednesday delivery were talked lower at $30.00-34.00 from $34.00-36.00 on Monday, the sources said.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP for Wednesday delivery also eased to near $17.00-19.00 from $20.00-22.50 on Monday.
February SPP was said to have fallen to $23.85-24.25 from $24.00-25.00 per MWh on Monday, the sources said.

Separately, Consumers Energy's 780 MW Palisades nuclear power plant in South Haven, Mich., was expected to begin electricity production Tuesday after a shutdown for repairs to main steam isolation valves.

Also, the 1,205 megawatt Perry nuclear power plant in North Perry, Ohio, was operating at full power as of early Tuesday following an electrical repair shutdown, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said.
IES Utilities has said it expects its 538 MW Duane Arnold nuclear power plant in Palo, Iowa to resume electricity production Thursday following a repair shutdown over the weekend.
